heading: Convert PDF to Grayscale
intro: Convert colored PDF pages to grayscale for black-and-white printing. Already-grayscale files are preserved; color pages are rendered as images, so file size can increase and their text may no longer be selectable.
faqs: Does grayscale conversion reduce file size?
Not always. Already-grayscale PDFs are preserved, while converting color pages to images can increase file size. Use Compress PDF when reducing size is your goal.
Will text remain selectable?
Text remains selectable when the source is already grayscale. Color pages are rendered to grayscale images and may need OCR before their text can be searched or copied.
Is the conversion reversible?
No. Once colored pages are converted to grayscale, their original color data is not recoverable from the output file.
Does it work on scanned PDFs?
Yes. Scanned image PDFs are fully supported and every embedded image is converted.

heading: Flatten PDF Form Fields
intro: Permanently bake all AcroForm field appearances into the page — essential for final submission, archiving, and preventing further editing.
faqs: What does flattening a PDF do?
Flattening converts interactive field widgets into static page content. The PDF looks the same but fields can no longer be typed in.
Can I unflatten a flattened PDF?
No. Flattening is permanent and irreversible. Keep the original fillable PDF before flattening.
Does flattening reduce file size?
Usually yes, as interactive form metadata and widget streams are removed.
